topic: Respiratory Balance Sheet, Amphibolic Pathway and Respiratory Quotient
title: How Many ATP From One Glucose? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Rice, ghee and dal are three very different foods, yet your cells burn all three in one shared pathway. Diya asks: how much energy does one sugar molecule really give, and does every food use oxygen the same way?

We zoom from a plant cell to a mitochondrion to its inner membrane, check the four assumptions behind the respiratory balance sheet, compare fermentation with aerobic respiration, follow fats and proteins into the amphibolic pathway, and measure the respiratory quotient for glucose, tripalmitin and protein with a pause and think. Then a worked example that counts the 38 ATP, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 90 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Three foods, one pathway
0:33 What is a balance sheet?
0:51 Zoom ladder: cell, mitochondrion, inner membrane
1:17 The four assumptions and 38 ATP
1:54 Fermentation vs aerobic respiration
2:21 The amphibolic pathway
3:04 Respiratory quotient + pause and think
4:05 Worked example: counting the 38 ATP
4:30 Exam trap: is it always 38 ATP?
4:52 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:22 Recap and three questions to answer
